findings.title: A tz-naive persisted timestamp raises on every cycle at three sibling loader seams (snapshots, curve, comfort)
findings.claim: With the stored timestamp written tz-naive, SnapshotRing.due, CurveLearner._step_down and ComfortLearner._decay raise TypeError on every call after load (21/21 heartbeats, 19/21 curve days, 21/21 comfort calls), and the #42 ring takes 0 snapshots instead of 3.
findings.mechanism: The loaders parse with datetime.fromisoformat and keep a naive value; consumers subtract it from an aware now. drift.Cusum.load (naive->UTC) and AccuracyTracker.from_dict lead_pending (drop naive) already guard the same leaf class; these three siblings do not. The heartbeat call site swallows at DEBUG, so the snapshot insurance, bias alarm and rollback stop permanently and silently; with comfort learning on, climate set_temperature raises after the write, and _record_quiet_comfort_period raises inside async_run_optimization's except-Exception (read, not reproduced end-to-end).

findings.title: A non-numeric snapshot temperature_bias makes best_restore raise and suppresses the accuracy_drift issue for good
findings.claim: For 4/4 JSON-legal non-numeric bias leaves ("0.3", "garbage", [0.3], {"v":0.3}) the restore_learned_snapshot service raises and 10 out-of-band days end with no accuracy_drift repair issue; 0/4 with a numeric leaf.
findings.mechanism: SnapshotRing.from_dict only checks each snapshot is a dict; best_restore calls np.isfinite(bias), which raises TypeError on str/list/dict (QuarantiningStore passes finite numeric strings through). On the alarm day the heartbeat raises before _create_issue; the latch is already set so observe_bias never reports a change again.

findings.title: One out-of-range DHW thermometer sample is booked as a physically impossible draw and inflates the published p90
findings.claim: A single -127 C sample on day 4 folds a 42.218 kWh draw occurrence (control 1.073) and raises the published window p90 from 1.073 to 25.760 kWh; 1e6 folds 231757 kWh.
findings.mechanism: async_learn_dynamics feeds the raw drop into async_fold_draw_stats (intensity*dt*thermal mass) with no plausibility bound; the occurrence stays in the 40-occurrence reservoir, and p90 is published as dhw_draw_stats.p90_kwh and, with DHW quantile targets on, becomes the plan's readiness energy.

findings.title: A timestamp stored while the clock ran ahead is trusted verbatim and stretches stale timeouts by the clock error
findings.claim: After a clock that ran 30 days ahead is corrected, the open-window latch release, the weekly snapshot and the curve step first act on days 33/37/31 instead of 4/8/2 (365 days ahead: 369/373/366).
findings.mechanism: Cusum.release_if_starved, SnapshotRing.due and CurveLearner._step_down compare now with a persisted time and never question one in the future; the vent latch it pins freezes every learner.

leads.what: The learner feed is unguarded inside the solve's except-Exception: any learner raise is logged as 'Optimization failed', bumps _solve_failures (towards the solve_failures repair issue) and skips _command_valve_target.

The heartbeat guard logs a permanent failure at DEBUG on every cycle. _async_load_accuracy runs its from_dict calls outside the try, so one raising parser aborts the rest of that store's load (dhw_accuracy, defrost, peaks, mode, comfort) in a fire-and-forget task.

Only the accuracy store's writer awaits QuarantiningStore.async_wait_for_read (:5153). The other stores' writers do not, although the loads are spawned fire-and-forget in __init__ (write-before-read clobber class, R6).
No physical bound on the energy of one occurrence: it accepts 231757 kWh (see D1-s1-03's harness).
No plausibility range for temperature readings, so the DS18B20 sentinel values -127 and 85 pass as ok readings to every learner.

The stub codec is stdlib json: it decodes 10**400 as an exact int and 1e400 as inf, and it writes NaN tokens. Real HA's orjson refuses or converts these, so store-fuzz results over-report loader raises (19 of 250 accuracy mutants were stub-only).
[carried by the orchestrator from RC2] the runtime fields it sets are not persisted and are lost at restart (user state that does not survive a restart; class of v2.4.1, v3.13.0, #1249, bug 5)

[carried by the orchestrator from R6 round 2] a save during startup, before the store's first read completes, can overwrite persisted learner state with defaults (the startup-clobber R6 fixed only in async_set_mode via async_wait_for_read)
